thesis.bull_case: TD Power Systems is executing strongly on its niche thesis — LTM revenue has reached ₹2,124 Cr with PAT margins stable at 12–14% and near-perfect (97%) CFO-to-PAT conversion confirming high earnings quality and no working-capital stress. The debt-free balance sheet, escalating dividend payouts (₹0.60 → ₹1.10 per share across four consecutive payments), and a face-value split collectively signal management's confidence in a durable earnings re-rating. With India's power-sector capex cycle visibly driving revenue acceleration from ₹452 Cr to ₹640 Cr over four quarters, the company's high-switching-cost niche in custom large electrical machines remains a potent structural tailwind.
thesis.bear_case: At PE 38x on LTM earnings of ₹275 Cr, the stock leaves no room for execution misses — a single quarter of order-book lumpiness or margin compression from copper/CRGO steel cost spikes on fixed-price contracts could trigger a sharp de-rating. The company's customer-concentration and dependence on domestic thermal and industrial capex means any policy reversal (accelerated renewables push crowding out thermal capex, project financing stress) would directly shrink the addressable order pipeline with no quick offset. Global OEMs (ABB Brush, Siemens Energy) with deeper R&D and balance sheets can selectively compete for marquee projects, capping long-run pricing power.
thesis.moat: Narrow but durable moat rooted in proprietary engineering design for large custom AC/DC electrical machines (>1 MVA), multi-year OEM supplier qualification cycles that create high switching costs, and a near-absence of domestic competitors in this sub-segment.
key_risks: Revenue and earnings lumpiness from large project-based contracts: a single order deferral can swing quarterly PAT by 20–30%, complicating re-rating at a 38x PE
Raw-material cost inflation (copper, CRGO steel) on fixed-price or semi-fixed contracts — unhedged exposure can compress margins sharply given ~12–14% net margin buffer

Concentration risk: a sustained slowdown in thermal-power or industrial capex (policy shifts to renewables, grid overcapacity, project-financing stress) would directly dent order inflows with no rapid product-mix alternative

facts.text: Face value split from ₹2 to ₹1 effective 24-Aug-2026 — typically signals management confidence in sustained stock re-rating and improves retail liquidity.

Four consecutive dividend payments across two financial years (₹0.60 interim → ₹0.65 final → ₹1.00 interim → ₹1.10 final), showing a clear escalating payout trend and strong free-cash-flow generation.
Debt-to-equity = 0.0 — entirely debt-free balance sheet, providing substantial headroom to fund working capital for a large order book without dilution or interest burden.
Quarterly financial data in the feed is all zero — this is a data-feed failure, not a company event; actual financials must be sourced directly from exchange filings before scoring thesis confidence.

Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) revenue of ₹640 Cr is the highest quarterly print in the dataset — up ~42% vs Q2 FY26 (₹452.5 Cr) and ~9% sequentially vs Q4 FY26 — confirming sustained revenue acceleration rather than a one-quarter spike.

Q1 FY27 CFO of ₹84.0 Cr against PAT of ₹86.3 Cr yields a 97% cash-conversion ratio, confirming that the revenue ramp is not creating working-capital stress or receivables build-up — earnings quality is high.

PAT margin has been stable in a narrow 12.3%–13.5% band across all four quarters despite significant revenue growth, indicating both operating leverage and cost discipline — no sign of competitive price pressure compressing economics.

3-year cumulative PAT growth of ~61.6% (~17.4% CAGR) is solid but the most recent quarterly cadence (PAT: ₹56 Cr → ₹60 Cr → ₹72 Cr → ₹86 Cr) suggests the growth rate is re-accelerating, implying the 3Y CAGR underrepresents forward earnings momentum.

Face-value split from ₹2 to ₹1 effective 24-Aug-2026, combined with four consecutive escalating dividends (₹0.60 → ₹0.65 → ₹1.00 → ₹1.10 per share pre-split adjusted), collectively signal management's conviction in sustained free-cash-flow generation and desire to broaden the retail investor base.
